perRailStateCounts.method: SELECT rail_key, cell_state->>'kind', count(*) FROM parcel_record_cell WHERE rail_key IN ('owner','utilityService','agValuation','maxImperviousCoverPct') GROUP BY 1,2, run directly against FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO on 2026-09-04. Total parcel population across all 6 program counties: 981,405.

owner.note: Tier 1 (cad_property, all 6 counties) plus Tier 2 (Williamson WCAD Owner override, subset of Tier 1's Williamson rows). Verified via the same per-rail-per-kind query pattern as the other rails; every county contributed a value-cell count consistent with that county's own parcel population, no unexplained unaccounted band outside expected cad_property gaps.

utilityService.note: Reported jointly with wave 1's close since both waves write the same rail via the same job (parcel-utility-service.mjs). electric=981405 (100%) confirms the HIFLD layer genuinely tiles the entire state, as Phase 1 scout predicted. water=0 is the same TWDB outage already named in wave 1's close -- not a wave-2 defect.

agValuation.note: Reported jointly with wave 1's close (same rail, same job, county-gated). Travis's contribution verified separately via a county_fips=48453-scoped sample after the FK-violation fix shipped and Travis's --apply re-ran clean; Travis's own value-cell count is consistent with TCAD's own reported ag-valuation-dataset row count for the county, within expected variance from parcels TCAD tracks but that were never instantiated in parcel_record (the same noParcelRecord class the FK fix now correctly counts and skips rather than crashing on).

maxImperviousCoverPct.note: Austin-only by design -- value cells exist only for parcels resolving to WATER SUPPLY SUBURBAN watershed classification (30%, LDC Sec. 25-8-423(B)); all other Austin parcels correctly left unaccounted (no code path fabricates a percentage for BSZ/SUBURBAN/URBAN/WATER SUPPLY RURAL). Every non-Austin parcel statewide is untouched by this rail, per its own explicit scope refuse (TRAVIS_FIPS=48453 guard in parcel-max-impervious-cover.mjs).

whatContradictedTheCard.finding: agValuation's real production FK violation (Postgres 23503) on Williamson's txgio_parcel 'PRIVATE ROAD' sentinel prop_id rows -- full detail in CP2. This directly contradicted the implicit assumption (never stated as a hard claim in the mission, but latent in the original wave-1 design) that every prop_id enumerated by this rail's own paging source corresponds to a real, instantiated parcel_record row. It does not. Fixed with a real existence check against the authoritative table, not a defensive try/catch around the symptom.

This wave's owner Tier 2 override initially raised a question (not a bug) of whether WCAD's quickrefid needed a crosswalk step the way WCAD's ag-valuation propertyid did in wave 1 -- verified directly (sampled and compared) that quickrefid IS the same key already in use, so no crosswalk was needed here. Named explicitly because the two WCAD datasets (Owner vs ag-valuation) turned out to use different key conventions from each other, which was not obvious in advance and is worth remembering if a future wave touches a third WCAD dataset.

scratch.text: 2026-09-04: real, independently-derived per-rail cell counts for owner/utilityService(electric)/agValuation(Travis)/maxImperviousCoverPct, queried directly from FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO -- see perRailStateCounts above.

A rail's own paging source (here, txgio_parcel) enumerating a prop_id is not proof that a corresponding parcel_record row was ever instantiated -- always existence-check against the authoritative table before writing a cell keyed off an external source's own ID space, not just against the ID's surface shape (e.g. 'looks like a real prop_id'). Sentinel/placeholder values like 'PRIVATE ROAD' are a real, recurring pattern in Texas CAD data, not a one-off.
Water CCN retry still pending TWDB recovery (shared with wave 1's leave_behind, same underlying outage). hoaDeedRestrictions scouted strong and is a good candidate to lead a future wave.
